title: kate-core: fold a line that a carriage return ends
summary: line_scalar treats a lone CR as a line break. A CR LF pair is one break. An LF-only fold stays the same range. The test goes in the existing view tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: view.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Change only line_scalar. A lone LF still starts the next line. A lone CR starts the next line. A CR LF pair is one break, and the next line starts after the LF. Do not count U+2028, VT, FF, or NEL. Do not write one arm for LF and another arm with the same step for CR. Do not write two if arms that return the same value. Combine them with ||. That is clippy::if_same_then_else. Update the doc sentence on line_scalar. The old sentence says each newline starts the next line. The new sentence says each line break starts the next line, and a CR LF pair is one break. You may update that sentence. Do not touch is_scrolled, apply_indent_folds, or offset_is_folded. The existing test apply_indent_folds_stores_char_ranges stays green. Do not rewrite its assertions. The test a_carriage_return_folds_like_a_newline builds a view the same way that test does. apply_indent_folds of a, CR, two spaces, b, CR with tab width 4 stores one range. The range is CharRange::new of Offset(1) and Offset(6). Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Stay inside this one behavior. Do not add VT, FF, NEL, or U+2028. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: view::tests::a_carriage_return_folds_like_a_newline
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. a CR, two spaces, b, CR has no fold. After the change the fold is Offset(1) through Offset(6). The LF fixture stays Offset(1) through Offset(6).
